```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B has a documented payer model in its category. Acquire.com charges sellers a $25-100/mo listing fee plus a 6-8% closing fee, and Flippa charges $29+ listings plus 5-10% success fees. A cites no one who has ever paid for Free Pascal/Lazarus documentation, and its own brief says the Foundation funds development, not docs.",
    "The 90-day goal is one paying customer, and B offers a path that does not depend on a deal closing. Upfront seller listing fees are an established charge in this category, and the DealMyApp comparable reports about 30 listings within two weeks. That suggests sellers will show up quickly. This is self-reported, and DealMyApp charges 0% commission, so it shows sellers will list, not that they will pay.",
    "A's demand evidence is complaints, not purchase intent. It rests on three quotes spread over 14 years (2010, about 2014, 2024) about scattered docs. The brief also concedes the real blocker may be maintainer unwillingness to engage with doc fixes, which an outside product cannot fix.",
    "A's addressable market is flagged by its own brief as too small to sustain revenue, and every incumbent (the wikis, official docs, PasDoc, Read the Docs' free OSS tier) is free. B's market is crowded, but it is a market with demonstrated transactions.",
    "B's risks are serious but specific: buyer-side liquidity, a $750 newsletter test that produced zero sales, and 0%-commission rivals. They mainly threaten long-term scale and closing-fee revenue, not the near-term possibility of a first paying seller. A's core risk, that no payer exists at all, directly blocks the 90-day goal."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's price hypothesis of a ~$50/month business tier. It is anchored only to Read the Docs Business pricing, a general-purpose docs host. Nothing in the brief shows that any company shipping Lazarus-based products has expressed willingness to pay for hosted or branded Pascal documentation, so the payer itself is speculative.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B's brief contains strong counter-evidence: five live competitors, three with 0% or near-0% commission that undercut fee-based models, a paid acquisition test with zero sales, and weak buyer conversion at the closest comparable, whose figures are self-reported. If 0%-fee rivals make listing fees untenable, B's 90-day payment path weakens considerably. Still, B shows people paying in the category and A shows none, which is the decisive difference for a first paying customer."
}
```
